disagreements.what_changed: Not an evidence conflict — r1's own parent correction row (census.tsv:129) already upgraded this row to SAFE(metadata-prune) candidate. r3 confirms that correction independently and adds the index/reachability checks above.
disagreements.error_in_r1_note: S22's note and the r1 defect D1 both assert that lore-shokunin's default branch is origin/master and that 28706dc is 'an ancestor of origin/master'. That is FALSE for this lane: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 28706dc origin/master` -> 'fatal: Not a valid object name origin/master' (rc=128), while the same check against origin/main -> rc=0, and `git branch -a --contains 28706dc` lists main + remotes/origin/main. r1's D1 wording over-generalises the fleet root's branch (origin/master) to all lanes.

disagreements.fleet_default_branch_is_mixed: Measured symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD across all lane repos: 12 are origin/master (chousa, kagi, kake, kama, kasegi, kengaku, kotoba, kumitate, mado, mori, tabi, tameshi, tsukuroi) and 7 are origin/main (audio, game-dev-2d, game-dev-3d, kaidoku, kotodama, lore, revenger); the fleet root is origin/master. A receipt procedure that hardcodes either name will produce false NOT-SAFE on roughly half the fleet. tools/souji-verify.sh handles this correctly (resolve_default_ref reads symbolic-ref origin/HEAD first, then falls back to a single origin/* ref, then refs/heads/master), which is why its verdict here is trustworthy. This refines r1's D1 rather than contradicting it.
disagreements.action_for_parent: If any r3 seat used a literal 'origin/main' or 'origin/master' for a pushed receipt, its NOT-SAFE may be a template artefact, not a finding. The shipped tool is the correct oracle.

disagreements.lane_hygiene_clause: AGENTS.md says 'never touch an artifact whose owning lane has dirty or unpushed work'. lore-shokunin currently has 3 commits on main ahead of origin/main (6cec83a, 1659a42, f553a27) and one untracked dir (.scratch/). A strict reading of that clause would yield NOT-SAFE. I record SAFE(metadata-prune) because (a) the binding tool spec's rule order is deterministic here, (b) the artifact being pruned is dead metadata whose every referenced object is reachable from refs (nothing is lost even though the lane is ahead of origin), and (c) round 1's parent correction and the r3 SCORECARD 'Planned' both pre-classify all 19 lore registrations as metadata-prune candidates. Parent's call whether the blanket clause should override the tool for this class.
